prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Medic survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved complete idle strip for this exact facing; it locks identity, camera and equipment grip. Image 2 is the original shipped single-facing seed. Both references show the required direction; do not invent an opposite-facing view. Preserve the same young adult woman Iona Vale with short wavy blonde hair and blue eyes under a large ivory hood, layered ragged ivory medical coat/cape, dark charcoal trousers, brown leather boots/harness, gloves, a rust-red medical satchel at the physical RIGHT hip and a small red-and-ivory vial next to it. The satchel retains its simple paired ivory bars and the upper sleeves their simple paired red bars. ONE long brass medical rifle with its red cylindrical reservoir stays in the physical RIGHT rear-trigger hand and LEFT forward-support hand. Preserve satchel side, the single rifle, reservoir, hood and face. No staff, second gun, duplicated satchel/vial, changed medical symbol, exposed hair on the back of the hood or new decorative pattern. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet color planes and selective practical contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive tiny scratches, decorative filigree or noise. Maintain two arms, two legs and one intact body/weapon in every pose.
Every pose faces EAST, screen RIGHT, in the exact approved side/three-quarter angle. Nose and both boots point screen RIGHT. Physical RIGHT is the near-side rear trigger arm; LEFT is the forward support arm. Do not exchange grips, turn the chest to face the viewer, or mirror the other facing.
Draw EXACTLY 6 full-body poses as one coherent dash sheet, arranged in a clear 3-column by 2-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. No additional figure. Action: One short grounded directional dodge: 1 full upright ready stance, 2 compress knees, 3 fast low weight-shift step, 4 compact transfer step, 5 plant/absorb the landing, 6 recover upright ready. Keep the same facing and camera in every pose. Keep BOTH hands securely on the SAME weapon with no new grip and only controlled cloth movement. No roll, somersault, huge leap, wing-like cape, clone, speed line, smoke or afterimage. Step screen RIGHT with the same east-facing side camera throughout. No torso twist toward the viewer.
Every pose is one complete independent drawn body at ONE common character scale calibrated from upright pose 1. Crouched and resting poses retain their naturally lower height. Use roomy clear gutters between all cells and generous padding around the ENTIRE body/weapon/cape, with a consistent ground baseline in each row. Genuine RGBA transparency: alpha zero outside each figure and between limbs/props. No floor, shadow, backdrop, haze, vignette, glow, particles, checker pattern, text, labels, frame numbers or grid lines. Keep a coherent animation rather than unrelated character illustrations.
